title: Indian-Origin Woman, 26, Shot Dead in Targeted Attack in Toronto
excerpt: Toronto police arrested 37-year-old Sharanjit Singh of Brampton and charged him with first-degree murder after Navneet Kaur was gunned down near Humberwood Boulevard. Her family alleges the accused had been harassing her after she rejected his marriage proposal.
body:
• Navneet Kaur, 26, was shot and killed on July 24 near Humberwood Boulevard and Rexdale Boulevard in Toronto; police pronounced her dead at the scene.
  • Sharanjit Singh, 37, of Brampton has been arrested and charged with first-degree murder and failure to comply with a release undertaking.
  • Kaur's family alleges the accused, a married man, had been harassing her after she repeatedly rejected his marriage proposal.
  • Her killing is the latest in a string of violent deaths of Indian nationals in Canada, following the fatal shooting of student Harsimrat Randhawa and the stabbing of Vidhi Meghani earlier this year.

A 26-year-old Indian-origin woman from Punjab, Navneet Kaur, was shot and killed on the morning of July 24 in what Toronto police have classified as a targeted attack. Officers responded to a shooting call at approximately 7:23 AM near Humberwood Boulevard and Rexdale Boulevard in the city's Rexdale neighbourhood, where they found Kaur outdoors with a gunshot wound. She was pronounced dead at the scene despite emergency medical intervention.

An eyewitness reported seeing Kaur being pursued by a man who shot her before fleeing. Police deployed drone units in the subsequent search and arrested 37-year-old Sharanjit Singh of Brampton. He has been charged with first-degree murder and failure to comply with a release undertaking, and was presented before the Ontario Court of Justice on July 25, according to Dainik Bhaskar.

Toronto police confirmed they consider the incident a targeted attack and said they do not believe any additional suspects are at large.

Family Alleges Harassment and Ignored Complaints

Kaur's family has painted a harrowing picture of the months leading up to her death. According to her cousin Malkeet Singh, the accused had known Kaur through their workplace in Canada but there was never any romantic relationship between them, Dainik Bhaskar reported.

https://x.com/HateDetectors/status/2081993888991268922

"He was already married and had children, yet he repeatedly pressured Navneet to marry him after divorcing his wife. When she refused, he began harassing and threatening her."

— Malkeet Singh, Navneet Kaur's cousin, to Dainik Bhaskar

The family said Kaur had lodged a complaint with Canadian police about the accused's alleged harassment. They also contacted the man's family in India to inform them of his behaviour. According to the family, his relatives admitted they were troubled by his conduct. The family believes the killing could have been prevented had authorities acted firmly on Kaur's complaint.

Fear for her safety had forced Kaur to return to Punjab two to three months before her death. After spending time with her family, she returned to Canada to resume her career — a decision that proved fatal.

A Disturbing Pattern

Kaur's killing is the latest in a string of violent deaths of Indian nationals in Canada that has rattled the diaspora community. In recent months, 21-year-old student Harsimrat Randhawa was killed by a stray bullet while waiting at a bus stop in Hamilton, Ontario. She was a student at Mohawk College and had no connection to the shooters — Hamilton Police described her as an "innocent bystander," according to Maha Media.

In May, 22-year-old Vidhi Meghani from Gujarat's Anand district was fatally stabbed in Ontario's Niagara region. Her father told news agency IANS that she was attacked by a drug dealer after refusing to pay him money. Meghani had been living in Canada for four years, studying business management.

A Punjab woman was also recently killed by her live-in partner in Canada, according to multiple Indian media reports.

Diaspora Anxiety Grows

The Consulate General of India in Toronto has expressed grief over the recent spate of killings. The pattern has fuelled anxiety among the more than 1.3 million members of Canada's Indian community, with families in India increasingly questioning whether sending their children abroad is worth the risk.

The case marks Toronto's 22nd homicide of 2026. Police have appealed for anyone with CCTV or dashcam footage from the Humberwood Boulevard area to come forward. Anonymous tips can be submitted through Crime Stoppers.

What's Next

Singh remains in custody following his court appearance. While police have classified the shooting as a targeted attack, the official motive has not been confirmed and the investigation remains active. The case is likely to intensify calls from the Indian diaspora community and Indian government officials for Canadian authorities to take stronger measures to protect Indian nationals living in the country.
image_caption: Toronto police launched a search after a 26-year-old Indian-origin woman was fatally shot in the Rexdale neighbourhood on July 24.
nri_angle: The killing adds to a growing list of violent deaths of Indian nationals in Canada, deepening anxiety among diaspora families and raising urgent questions about whether complaints of harassment and threats are being adequately addressed by Canadian authorities.
author: Diaspora Desk
